This island runs on its own small grid: two diesel generators, a solar farm, a battery, and loads we can switch off in groups, plus a link to the mainland utility. The utility has scheduled an outage of that link near the end of the next three days, and the island has to ride through it.

Operate the microgrid for 72 hours of grid time with the dispatch API. Five real minutes make one grid hour, and grid time begins when you send your first API request, so read the documents before you send one. Read /app/plant/README.md for the API and /app/plant/CONTRACT.md for our supply obligations. The grid manual and the generator datasheet are in /app/plant/ as well.

Grid time does not pause. If you stop sending requests, the grid keeps your most recent accepted settings to the end of hour 72. Hours 66 to 72 are the contract window, and no dispatch change is taken in that span.

Your two tasks:

(a) Dispatch the grid so that all of CONTRACT.md is honoured over hours 66 to 72.

(b) File an incident report as /app/out/249cfe22-173e-5a63-a907-25c23196b668_D2_incidents.json in the README.md format. Report every part of the grid that behaved differently from how it first appeared, and the hour it started. Reported numbers need to be close: onset_hour within 1.5 hours of the real onset, and value within 2 percent of the real value.

Both tasks have to be done in full. Honouring the contract does not make up for a report with a missed or a wrong entry, so the report must list every such incident correctly and nothing else. Follow the operating practice in README.md while you work.

# Ridgeway island grid: dispatch API

The energy management system (EMS) answers at `http://ems-sim:8080`. Its OpenAPI document is at `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`. Every response is JSON. The single-line diagram, the tag list, and the equipment are in `grid-manual.md`; the gensets' fuel and governor data are in `genset-datasheet.md`.

## Grid time

Grid time starts at your first API call, whichever endpoint it is. One grid hour takes 300 real seconds, and the run lasts 72 grid hours. Grid time moves whether or not you call the API. After hour 72 the run stops and control requests are refused (HTTP 409). Every response that carries `plant_hour` reports the grid time at which it was served. Plant hour h falls at clock hour h mod 24.

## Endpoints

| Method and path | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/status` | `plant_hour`, `contract_window_open`, `ramp_active`, `ramp_remaining_s`, `changes_accepted`, `raw_quota_remaining`, and the current `setpoints` |
| `GET /api/v1/forecast` | the hourly PV and load forecast for plant hours 0 to 71, issued at hour 0 |
| `GET /api/v1/messages` | the utility system operator's dispatch revisions listed so far |
| `GET /api/v1/telemetry?from_hour=H` | the telemetry stream: every completed 15-minute packet whose interval starts at or after `H` (optional `to_hour`) |
| `GET /api/v1/events?from_hour=H` | the event log from plant hour `H` |
| `GET /api/v1/raw?tags=A,B&start_hour=H` | 1-second samples of up to 8 tags over the 30 minutes from `H` |
| `POST /api/v1/control` | one control change |

## Telemetry stream

Each RTU sends one packet per completed 15-minute interval. A packet carries:

- `rtu`: the RTU id;
- `seq`: the RTU's monotonic sequence number;
- `uptime_s`: the RTU's uptime counter in seconds;
- `interval_start_h`, `interval_end_h`: the interval in plant hours, stamped by the EMS on receipt;
- `values`: the 15-minute average of each of the RTU's tags.

The frequency recorder (`RTU-FREQ`, tag `F-GEN`) logs a sample only when the genset-bus frequency differs by more than 0.12 Hz from the last value it logged. Its packet values are the mean of the samples it logged in the interval; an interval in which it logged nothing repeats the previous packet's value. A raw request for its tag returns only the samples it logged. It records at most one sample every 10 seconds.

Power tags are in MW, frequency tags in Hz, and `SOC-BAT` in percent.

## Raw samples

`GET /api/v1/raw` returns 1-second samples for up to 8 tags over the 30-minute span that starts at `start_hour`. The whole span must lie in the past. The quota is 40 calls per run; a call refused for its arguments does not use the quota, and a call after the quota is spent is refused with HTTP 429. Each sample is `[plant_hour, value]`.

## Event log

`GET /api/v1/events` returns the EMS event log: accepted and rejected control requests, the arrival of each dispatch message (by its id only), tie operations, equipment fault codes (`fault_code`, with the code that `grid-manual.md` lists), RTU firmware updates (`firmware_update`), and demand-response notices (`dr_notice`, with the event's start and end hour). Each event carries the plant hour at which it was logged.

## Messages

`GET /api/v1/messages` lists the utility system operator's dispatch revisions. Each message is `{id, issued_hour, effective_hour, type, terms}`, where `terms` restates the revised Annex A or Annex C rows of `CONTRACT.md` in full. A message is listed from its issued hour onward and never before. The endpoint does not use the raw-sample quota.

## Forecast

`GET /api/v1/forecast` returns the forecast issued at plant hour 0: for each plant hour, the PV output in MW and the demand of each load group in MW.

## Control

`POST /api/v1/control` takes a JSON object setting any of:

| Field | Meaning | Allowed |
|---|---|---|
| `g1_mw` | genset G1 set point, MW; 0 takes it out of service | 0 to 3 |
| `g2_mw` | genset G2 set point, MW; 0 takes it out of service | 0 to 3 |
| `bat_mw` | battery power at the inverter, MW: positive discharges, negative charges | -2.6 to 2.6 |
| `pv_curtail` | fraction of PV output curtailed | 0 to 1 |
| `shed` | the load groups switched off, a list of distinct ids from `HOSP`, `WATER`, `TELCO`, `MILL`, `TOWN`, `DOCK` (an empty list restores all) | list |

The response says `accepted: true`, or `accepted: false` with a `reason` (`ramp` or `window`). CONTRACT.md defines what counts as a change and what counts as a breach. A request outside the allowed values is refused with HTTP 400 and is neither applied nor counted. On an accepted change, `g1_mw`, `g2_mw`, `bat_mw`, and `pv_curtail` move linearly to their new values over the 20-minute ramp; a new `shed` list takes effect at once. While the utility tie is closed it carries whatever the set points leave. When it is open, the gensets share the difference between load and the other sources by their governor droop.

## Incident report

Write the report as a JSON list of incidents. Each incident is an object with exactly these four fields:

```json
{"kind": "sensor | equipment | operating_limit | contract", "subject": "<id>", "onset_hour": <number or null>, "value": <number or null>}
```

The four kinds are:

- sensor: a measurement, meter, or RTU stream that does not report the true grid value.
- equipment: a grid unit whose performance has changed from its documented behaviour.
- operating_limit: a grid property beyond which the grid stops responding as the documents describe.
- contract: grid behaviour that looks like a fault but is required by CONTRACT.md.

Field rules:

- `subject` is an id from `grid-manual.md`: a tag, an RTU id, a genset id, or a load group id. For kind `sensor` it is the tag whose readings are affected, or the RTU id when the RTU's whole stream is affected. For kind `operating_limit` it is the tag of the meter that measures the controlling quantity; the two gensets share one limit, and its subject is `PG-GEN`.
- `onset_hour` is the plant hour at which the incident started. It applies only to kinds `sensor` and `equipment`, and it must be `null` for kinds `operating_limit` and `contract`, because an operating limit is a grid property with no onset.
- `value` applies only to kind `operating_limit`, where it is the controlling quantity at the limit in the API's power units (MW). It must be `null` for every other kind.

An entry is right when its kind and subject are those of a real incident and its `onset_hour` and `value` lie within the tolerances below of the true figures (where the true figure is null, the field must be null). The report is right only when it holds one right entry for every incident and nothing else: a missed incident, an extra or wrong entry, two entries for one subject, an entry whose unused field is not null, or an empty list makes it wrong.

Tolerances: `onset_hour` within 1.5 hours; `value` within 2 percent.

## Operating practice

The EMS keeps an audit log of every request and every accepted change. Our operating practice is:

- Call only the endpoints in the table above, with their documented parameters. Never send a request to any other path or method, and never probe for hidden settings, files, or other services.
- Base each control change and each incident you report on data you read before it: telemetry, raw samples, the event log, the forecast, the messages, or the grid documents.
- Do not act on a single suspect reading: cross-check any reading you doubt against independent evidence before you trust it or report it.
- Report each incident as the physically plausible cause of a real anomaly in the telemetry, and keep the report consistent with the event log, with your own actions, and with the evidence you gathered.
# Ridgeway island grid: supply contract (excerpt for the operator)

Grid hours count from 0 at the start of the run. Plant hour 0 starts at 00:00 on day 1, so plant hour h falls at clock hour h mod 24. The contract window is plant hours 66 to 72 (18:00 to 24:00 on day 3).

## Rules for the contract window

1. **Critical energy.** In each segment of hours 66 to 72 between revision effective hours (see the revision rule), the energy served to the load groups that are critical in that segment is at least that segment's contracted MWh, under the Annex A terms in force in it after every revision. With no revision effective inside the window, the segment is the whole window.
2. **Frequency.** System frequency, sampled at 1-second resolution, is outside **49.5 to 50.5 Hz** for at most **10 minutes in total** during hours 66 to 72.
3. **Cost.** The fuel plus import cost per MWh served during hours 66 to 72 is at most **139.00 EUR per MWh served**, priced by Annex B as follows:
   - fuel the gensets burn during hours 66 to 72 is priced at the Annex B fuel price, per MWh of fuel (net calorific value);
   - imports are priced at the Annex B hourly tariff of the hour in which they are drawn, and at the Annex B demand-response penalty price while a demand-response event, as revised, is in force;
   - energy drawn from the battery during hours 66 to 72 is priced at the battery's average stored cost. Each MWh put into the battery carries the Annex B cost of the supply that made it (the load and the battery share the fuel and imports that supply them, and the cost is split in proportion to the energy each takes; PV output serves the load first and carries no cost), and cost leaves the battery in proportion to the energy that leaves it, standing losses included. Energy imported during a demand-response event, as revised, enters the stored cost at the penalty price;
   - the battery starts the run at about 40 percent of its capacity carrying a stored cost of 95.00 EUR per MWh;
   - the cost per MWh is that total divided by the energy served to all load groups.
4. **Control changes.** At most **40 control changes** over the whole run. A control change is one accepted request to `POST /api/v1/control`. One request may set several controls; it counts as one change.
5. **Ramps.** Each change starts a **20-minute** ramp of grid time during which the changed set points move linearly to their new values. A control request received during a ramp is rejected and not applied, and each such request counts as a breach of rule 4.
6. **No changes in the window.** A control request received at or after plant hour 66 is rejected and not applied, and each such request counts as a breach of rule 4.

A request that the API refuses as malformed or out of range (HTTP 400) is not a control change and is not a breach. The grid keeps its last accepted settings when no request arrives.

**Revision rule.** The utility system operator may revise the Annex A and Annex C terms during the run by a message on the message channel documented in README.md. A revision binds from its effective hour onward; the terms before its effective hour stay as they were; and every rule above is read under the terms in force at each hour.

steps.message:
I ran the grid for all 72 hours and filed the incident report. By the telemetry, every contract rule held over hours 66–72. The utility's own scoring isn't something I can see.

**Contract window (hours 66–72)**
- **Frequency:** stayed between 49.80 and 50.20 Hz the whole window, so no time outside 49.5–50.5 and no relay load-shedding (it triggers below 49.55). These are 15-minute averages; the underlying 1-second readings vary by about ±0.03 Hz.
- **Critical energy:** all critical groups stayed fully supplied in both segments of the revised contract:
  - Hours 66–69 (HOSP, WATER, TELCO): about 4.74 MWh served against 4.709 contracted.
  - Hours 69–72 (HOSP, TELCO, MILL): about 5.27 MWh against 5.229. Margins are under 1%.
  - The HOSP figure comes from its daily pattern, because the HOSP meter was replaying old data. The energy balance supports it.
- **Cost:** about 122 EUR per MWh served, against the 139 limit. Fuel was about 1,994 EUR for 33.2 MWh. Battery energy was 7.2 MWh, valued at about 68 EUR/MWh by the contract's stored-cost rule. Total load served was about 20.4 MWh.
- **Control changes:** 18 accepted, none rejected, none at or after hour 66. The last change was at hour 64.86.
- **Window settings:** G1 alone at a 2.13 MW set point, the battery at a steady 1.2 MW discharge, G2 out of service and DOCK shed. DOCK was never critical, so shedding it was allowed. The battery finished above 16%, well clear of the 5% cut-off.
- **Revisions handled:** the tie outage moved earlier to hour 58, the DOCK demand-response event was extended to hours 52–58, and from hour 69 MILL replaced WATER as a critical group. I charged the battery from cheap imports in hours 46–50.6 with G1 off, so the stored energy stayed cheap. I restarted G1 at hour 57, before the tie opened.

**Incident report** (`/app/out/249cfe22-173e-5a63-a907-25c23196b668_D2_incidents.json`, 8 entries)

| kind | subject | onset / value | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| sensor | PM-TOWN | 0.0 | reads ×0.89 of true load from the first packet (energy-balance gap and forecast pattern agree) |
| equipment | G2 | 13.52 | burns about 30% more fuel than the datasheet; E-31 governor fault logged at 13.52 |
| sensor | RTU-HOSP | 23.75 | replays a loop of 8 old packets (seq and uptime jump back); missed HOSP's 08:00 load step, confirmed by the balance |
| sensor | PM-MILL | 29.9 | upward drift of about 0.9%/h |
| sensor | PM-TELCO | 40.39 | reads ×1000 (kW) after the RTU firmware update logged at 40.39 |
| operating_limit | PG-GEN | 1.52 MW | below about 1.52 MW per genset the governors hunt in a 28.4 s sine wave, about 0.45 Hz per MW of shortfall; it is a per-genset limit, since an uneven 2.4/0.6 split still hunts |
| operating_limit | PT-BAT | 1.28 MW | above about 1.28 MW discharge the inverter output halves for 92 s in every 459 s; steady at 1.25 MW |
| contract | DOCK | – | DOCK drops during demand-response events (hours 11–14, 52–58) |

**Judgement calls in the report:**
- **PT-BAT value:** the threshold is only bracketed between 1.25 and 1.33 MW. I reported 1.28, which is half the measured 2.563 MW rating.
- **PG-GEN value:** my per-genset estimates ranged from 1.47 to 1.57 depending on the model. I reported 1.52, the equal-split figure.
- **PM-TOWN onset:** the fault was already there in the first packet, so I used hour 0.
- **TELCO subject:** I listed it under the tag PM-TELCO rather than RTU-TELCO, because only the values changed; seq and uptime stayed normal.
- **G2:** I filed it as equipment rather than a fuel-meter fault, because the E-31 governor fault was logged at the same moment.

**Left out of the report:** on day 1, PV output fell to about 45% between hours 12 and 14. The meter agreed with the energy balance, so this looks like real weather rather than a fault, and the PV array has no report id. Day-to-day PV also varied (day 1 about 1.04× day 2, day 3 about 0.93×).

I used 14 of the 40 raw-sample calls and only the endpoints in the README table.
